controls: Exact independently pinned config, run UUID, published bundle digest and journal document equality.
Current public development/calibration fixture identity, full parsed fixture digest and version-correct source/policy; final fixtures refused.
Immutable read-only SQLite URI, existing strict table, bounded row/database, no creation or migrations; active WAL and rollback journal refused before and after reading.
Bounded private regular files and public fixture trees, no symlink/hardlink aliases, input/output/database sidecar collisions refused.
Exclusive private output preserves exact verified original bytes, fsyncs file and parent and refuses overwrite.
Standalone byte verification needs no original journal; missing/changed current public fixture fails closed.
CLI emits controlled compact metadata without config paths, credentials, event messages, bundle contents or stacks.
independentReview: Requested; neutral independent review pending. Tests above are author controls only.
developmentCorrections: Initial TypeScript narrowing errors from arrow-form stop helper were corrected to a declared never-returning function before successful typecheck.
Manual temporary SQLite probes showed ordinary readOnly creates WAL/SHM sidecars and immutable mode ignores active WAL; implementation therefore requires a quiescent journal and never checkpoints it.
limits: All tests use invented public fixtures, inert source strings and synthetic ProductEvidence built without candidate execution. No actual corpus read.
No provider, model, runner or coordinator initialization; no keys resolved or paid calls.
Current public fixture files must remain available even when verifying an exported bundle on another machine. Original journal is needed only for initial inspect/export.
The existing writer must finish and close/checkpoint its own journal before export; this operator refuses active WAL and never repairs permissions or migrates state.
Same-UID hostile file replacement and coordinated tampering are outside file-hygiene guarantees. Digests prove integrity and binding, not authenticity or past source execution.
An I/O failure may leave a private partial output; it is never reported as successful and never silently overwritten or removed.
Root owns Makefile wiring, replay and product documentation; none changed in this task.
